articles.title: Buying a home seems impossible. Here’s what Boomers just don’t understand
articles.summary: A $429,100 median home price at 7.40% mortgage rates tells only part of the story when down payments now equal nearly a full year's household income.
articles.body: Whenever someone complains about today's mortgage rates, somebody inevitably says: "You think 7.5% is bad? I paid 14% in the 1980s!" They're right about the interest rate. But they're missing the bigger problem. GEN Z IS WORKING HARD, BUT THE ECONOMY IS PUTTING THE AMERICAN DREAM OUT OF REACH FOR MANY Today's homebuyers aren’t just fighting a 7% mortgage. They're fighting high rates on a home price that has grown much faster than the amount sitting in their checking account. Look at the numbers. A PROBLEM HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT IS KEEPING AMERICANS FROM BUYING HOMES In 1984, the median new home sold for about $79,900, while the median household income was roughly $22,400. That's a home-price-to-income ratio of about 3.6 times income. The average 30-year mortgage rate that year was a painful 13.9%. Now fast-forward. AMERICA'S HOUSING MARKET COULD RUN OUT OF SOMETHING MORE IMPORTANT THAN HOMES By 1990, the ratio had climbed to about 4.1 times income, with the median new home costing $122,900. In 2000, it remained around 4 times income, even with mortgage rates still above 8%. Then housing prices really started separating from paychecks. GEN Z DEMOCRATIC LAWMAKER SPARS WITH BABY BOOMERS OVER WHETHER AMERICAN DREAM IS DEAD By 2010, the median new home cost roughly 4.5 times the median household income. By 2020, it was approaching 5 times income or $330,900 for the house versus roughly $68,000 in household income. When someone says, "We had 14% mortgages in the 1980s, and we still bought houses," they're leaving out half the story. WE MUST HELP MORE PEOPLE BUY A HOME. IT’S KEY TO THE AMERICAN DREAM Homes were much cheaper relative to what families earned. In 1984, the median new home sold for about $79,900, while the median household income was roughly $22,400. That's a home-price-to-income ratio of about 3.6 times income. The average 30-year mortgage rate that year was a painful 13.9%. And here's where it gets ugly The median existing home price was $429,100 in August 2026. The latest median household income figure is $87,460 for 2025. That's about 4.9 times household income. Meanwhile, the average 30-year mortgage rate hit 7.40% on Oct. 8. So yes, your parents may have had a 14% mortgage. But they didn't have a $429,000 house attached to it. $104,200 SALARY IN ORANGE COUNTY, CALIFORNIA CONSIDERED 'LOW-INCOME' BY STATE OFFICIALS Then there's the down payment This may be the part nobody talks about enough. A 20% down payment on that $79,900 home in 1984 was about $16,000. Today, 20% down on a $429,100 home is nearly $86,000. That's almost an entire year's median household income before closing costs, moving expenses, furniture or the first trip to The Home Depot. In 1984, the 20% down payment represented about 71% of median household income. Today, it's roughly 98%. That's a gigantic pile of cash for a first-time buyer to accumulate while simultaneously paying rent, student loans, car payments, insurance and everyday living expenses. And then you still have the mortgage Put 20% down on today's $429,100 home, and you're borrowing about $343,000. At 7.28%, the principal-and-interest payment alone is roughly $2,350 per month. Then add property taxes, homeowners' insurance, HOA fees and maintenance. That's why simply telling young people to "stop buying $7 coffees" completely misses the point. Coffee isn't the problem. The math is. When someone says, "We had 14% mortgages in the 1980s, and we still bought houses," they're leaving out half the story. Today's buyers are getting squeezed from three directions at once: home prices relative to income, the cash required to get in the door and the cost of borrowing once they get there. Yes, mortgage rates were worse in the 1980s. But affordability isn't about one number. articles.title: Nick Jonas co-founded a diabetes nonprofit that created 8,400 insulin-access plans in 2025; how its US programme helps people find affordable treatment
articles.summary: Access to affordable insulin remains a challenge for people living with diabetes in the US, particularly those who struggle with insurance coverage or the
articles.body: Access to affordable insulin remains a challenge for people living with diabetes in the US, particularly those who struggle with insurance coverage or the cost of prescriptions. Singer Nick Jonas, who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 13, has helped address this problem through Beyond Type 1, the diabetes nonprofit he co-founded. Its GetInsulin programme connects people with financial assistance and savings options suited to their circumstances. According to the organisation’s 2025 Impact Report, the initiative created 8,400 personalised insulin-access plans during the year, with treatment costing almost always $35 a month or less.Nick Jonas’s insulin-access programme helps people find affordable treatmentBeyond Type 1 introduced GetInsulin in 2020 to help Americans find ways to obtain insulin when its price becomes difficult to manage. As explained in the organisation’s article, Nick Jonas launched an initiative to increase access to affordable insulin. Jonas joined forces with the nonprofit to develop a free online search tool that helps people identify available assistance.The initiative was designed around a practical problem. People who need insulin may find themselves facing high pharmacy bills, uncertain insurance coverage or difficulty identifying programmes that could reduce their expenses. Finding the right option can involve navigating different eligibility rules and application processes.GetInsulin aims to make that search simpler by bringing relevant information together. Instead of requiring users to investigate numerous programmes independently, the website asks for a few details and generates a personalised action plan.The original launch also involved collaboration with the NAACP and Feeding America, according to Beyond Type 1’s 2020 announcement. The initiative reflected an effort to make information about affordable insulin more accessible to people who might otherwise struggle to find support.The programme builds on Jonas’s personal experience with diabetesJonas’s involvement in diabetes advocacy is closely connected to his own diagnosis. Beyond Type 1’s official profile of the singer states that he was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at 13. Alongside his career in music and acting, he has supported causes involving health, education, human rights and young people.Type 1 diabetes requires people to manage their condition with insulin. For those who depend on the medication, being unable to afford a prescription can create an immediate problem.Beyond Type 1’s announcement about the initiative described insulin access as a human rights issue. That approach places affordability at the centre of the discussion, recognising that people should be able to seek treatment without facing financial barriers that put their health at risk.The programme does not remove every obstacle associated with healthcare costs. Instead, it offers a way to identify existing assistance and understand which options may fit an individual's situation.What did Beyond Type 1 achieve with its insulin programme in 2025The organisation’s 2025 Impact Report highlights the scale of the programme’s work. During the year, GetInsulin helped generate 8,400 personalised action plans intended to improve access to insulin. Beyond Type 1 reported that the resulting options almost always made insulin available for $35 a month or less.The report also describes a change in how the initiative supports users. Beyond Type 1 introduced a new email journey for GetInsulin and expanded its media support, moving towards ongoing guidance rather than relying solely on one-time assistance.This distinction matters because a person’s financial or insurance circumstances can change. Someone who finds a suitable programme initially may still need information and support to maintain access over time. Continued guidance can help users revisit their options as their needs evolve.The figure of 8,400 represents personalised plans created, rather than a confirmed count of individual prescriptions filled or people who received insulin directly from the nonprofit. The organisation’s reported results demonstrate the reach of its information and referral service while distinguishing that work from the actual supply of medication.The impact report also places the programme within Beyond Type 1’s broader work during 2025, which included expanding its international activities and supporting the diabetes community through education and advocacy.The online tool matches users with assistance based on their needsThe Get Insulin programme page explains how the service works. Users answer questions about their location, insurance status, income and insulin prescription. The information helps the platform identify options that may be suitable for their circumstances.The service covers people with different insurance arrangements, including those who are uninsured, under-insured or insured but still facing unaffordable costs. It is available in English and Spanish and is intended for people living with diabetes in the US.Beyond Type 1 also separates the service into 2 routes. Urgent Insulin Support is designed for people who have fewer than 7 days of insulin remaining and may be at risk of rationing their supply. It directs users towards possible options offered through insulin manufacturers.Continuing Need Insulin Support is intended for people whose prescribed insulin has become too expensive at the pharmacy. It helps them build a personalised plan for more reliable access throughout the year. The distinction allows people to look for help according to the urgency of their circumstances.The quick-start guide explains how people can use the serviceBeyond Type 1’s GetInsulin quick-start guide outlines the information users should gather before beginning. This includes their state and ZIP code, insurance arrangements and insulin brand or prescription.Location is important because some US states have limits on insulin co-payments. The guide notes that certain state caps range from $35 to $100 for a 30-day supply. The options available to an individual can depend on where they live and the type of coverage they have.Once users begin the process, they can follow the website’s prompts to build an action plan. Providing an email address and preferred pharmacy is optional, although these details can make it easier to revisit the plan later. Users can also receive a copy by email.There is an important limitation, however. GetInsulin is neither a pharmacy nor an insurance plan. Beyond Type 1 does not dispense or ship insulin through the service, and the website cannot guarantee that every user will qualify for a particular assistance programme. Instead, it connects people with possible sources of savings and support.For anyone struggling to pay for a prescription, the service provides a starting point for exploring available options and reducing the time spent searching for help.You use AI every day. articles.title: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar joined US Army as lieutenant colonel in 2025; his job: find coders that Army doesn’t know it has and turn them into...
articles.summary: Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar has a second job in the US Army Reserve, and it has little to do with weapons or battlefield software.
articles.body: Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar has a second job in the US Army Reserve, and it has little to do with weapons or battlefield software. Speaking to CBS News on Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan, Sankar said his main role as a lieutenant colonel is helping the Army find soldiers who can code, and then making sure that talent is put to proper use.Sankar works with the Army’s G-1, the department that handles personnel and human resources. The problem he described is structural. The Army has skilled programmers in its ranks, but its career system was built for an industrial-era military, a model Sankar likened to Napoleonic codes. A soldier at the E-4 grade, a junior enlisted rank, could be an exceptional coder and still have no clear path to doing that work in uniform.Why the US Army struggles to use its tech talentSankar told CBS News that “the Army is drowning in talent,” referring to uniformed soldiers who know how to write code. The catch is that their skills don’t follow rank. The Army assigns roles by seniority, but coding ability doesn’t come with stripes.His work focuses on three questions. How does the Army spot these soldiers, how does it stop them from getting lost in the system, and how does it place them on projects that use what they can do? The goal is to turn them into assets the military draws on instead of leaving them in roles unrelated to their skills.What is Detachment 201, the Army’s tech executive corpsSankar was sworn in in June 2025 as part of Detachment 201, the Army’s Executive Innovation Corps. The name nods to HTTP status code 201, which signals that a new resource has been created on a server. The first cohort included Meta’s Andrew Bosworth and two executives with OpenAI roots, Kevin Weil and Bob McGrew. Army officials have credited Sankar with pitching the idea and recruiting the other three.The executives serve around 120 hours a year and hold the rank of lieutenant colonel because of their private-sector expertise. They were spared basic training but still face fitness tests and marksmanship training.The arrangement has raised questions about conflicts of interest. Brennan pointed out that Palantir holds billions of dollars in US government contracts. Sankar said the Defense Department’s lawyers manage this closely, and that reservists can only work on projects where they have no conflict.He also spoke about why he signed up. Sankar’s family fled violence in Lagos when he was a child, and he called serving in the US military the greatest honour. He said his late father would have loved to see him attend a service academy. Now 44, he said he hopes he has more to give the country today than he did at 24.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Man denies racist murder of scientist in Dundee
articles.summary: Kyler Rattray, 21, is alleged to have repeatedly struck Dr Fortune Gomo with a knife last year.
articles.body:
A man has denied the racially-aggravated murder of a scientist on a Dundee street.

Kyler Rattray, 21, is accused of attacking Dr Fortune Gomo in South Street in July last year.

Prosecutors allege the 39-year-old academic was repeatedly struck on the body with a knife and that the attack was aggravated by prejudice relating to race, colour nationality or ethnicity.

The trial is due to begin on 5 January 2028 at the High Court in Dundee and is expected to last eight days.

Rattray also faces a separate charge of illegally having a knife in a public place.

The case called at a virtual hearing at the High Court in Glasgow earlier.

Dr Gomo was found fatally injured on the street and was treated by paramedics at the scene, but never recovered.

At the time, Police Scotland acknowledged that her death had caused great shock throughout Dundee.

She was originally from Mutare in eastern Zimbabwe, had graduated with a PhD from Dundee University, and had recently started working for Scottish Water.

articles.title: America's best pizzerias crowned in new rankings on Columbus Day as pizza expert shares skepticism
articles.summary: A New York City pizzeria tops the 50 Top Pizza list for 2026, but a pizza expert and historian tells Fox News Digital that the organization leans toward certain styles.
articles.body: Columbus Day commemorates a famous voyage across the Atlantic, but Americans don't have to travel nearly as far to discover some of the country's best pizza. The 50 Top Pizza rankings of 2026 highlight restaurants from coast to coast, though what makes a pie worthy of the top spot is still a matter of taste. New Haven, Connecticut-based food historian and pizza expert Colin Caplan told Fox News Digital that what constitutes the "best" pizza really comes down to personal preference. AMERICA'S BEST-TASTING PIZZA CHAIN IS AN OLD-SCHOOL FAVORITE, SURVEY FINDS Ranked lists such as those published by 50 Top Pizza are helpful for expanding palates and introducing people to restaurants and dishes to try, he noted, but there's usually some subjectivity at play. "50 Top Pizza is a very well-respected Italian-based, chef-based site that really goes and finds what they think is the best," he said, but suggested the organization might have a slight bias toward certain pizza styles that align with its Italian roots, such as Neapolitan. Ultimately, though, good pizza is all about the love that goes into it. "If the heart is [in] it, the pizza is going to taste amazing," Caplan said. These are the top five pizzerias in America for 2026, according to 50 Top Pizza. 1. Una Pizza Napoletana — New York City Founded in 1996 by Anthony Mangieri, this New York City pizzeria has "a stand-up example of sit-down pizza," according to The New York Times. AMERICA'S MOST AND LEAST EXPENSIVE PLACES TO ORDER PIZZA REVEALED IN NEW STUDY Eater NY called the Margherita pie "a miracle of pizza development and evolution unlike any other Neapolitan pie in the world." Mangieri personally makes each ball of dough by hand, the website says, and he shapes, tops and bakes every pizza himself. This is the fifth year in a row that Una Pizza Napoletana has claimed the top spot in the 50 Top Pizza USA ranking. The restaurant also placed second in the 50 Top Pizza World 2026 ranking. 2. (Tie) Pizzeria Sei — Los Angeles and Tony's Pizza Napoletana — San Francisco Operated by chef William (Sang Woo) Joo and his wife and partner, Jennifer So, Pizzeria Sei has been serving Tokyo-style Neapolitan pizzas since 2022. RETRO PIZZA HUT DRAWS CUSTOMERS FROM HOURS AWAY AS 1980S NOSTALGIA SENDS SALES SOARING The crusts are shaped using a crimping technique that, along with a quick baking time at high heat, leads to a unique, varied texture, the website states. Tied for second place is Tony's Pizza Napoletana, a San Francisco establishment run by 13-time world pizza champion Tony Gemignani. In addition to Neapolitan, Tony's serves multiple styles of pizza, including Detroit, Sicilian, New York and Romana, among others. The pizzeria also placed fifth in the 2026 50 Top Pizza World ranking. 3. Razza — Jersey City, New Jersey Chef and owner Dan Richer, a 2011 James Beard Foundation Rising Star Chef semifinalist, opened Razza in 2007. The pizzeria garnered a three-star review in 2017 from The New York Times, and in 2019 it was given the distinction of Best Pizza in North America by 50 Best. "Each ingredient is hand-picked, down to the salt that goes on the pizza," according to its website. Both the bread and butter are made in-house, the flour is milled nearby in Clifton, N.J., and a homegrown yeast culture is added to the crust. 4. Truly Pizza – Dana Point, California Founded by Donna Baldwin and John Arena, Truly Pizza focuses on using fresh, seasonal ingredients and supporting local farmers. At the two-story, open-air Dana Point location, guests can enjoy coastal scenery while dining on artisan pizzas — both round and square — ranging from classic cheese to umami mushroom. Situated in the Miami neighborhood of Wynwood, the restaurant offers a wide range of pizzas, from the tomato-forward Assoluto di Pomodoro, featuring San Marzano tomato mousse and roasted cherry tomato cream, to the Fior di Zucca Al Quadrato, which has zucchini cream and squash blossoms. articles.title: Teenager arrested after two teachers shot in French school
articles.summary: A 14-year-old was detained after the middle-school principal and teacher were injured.
articles.body:
A pupil has been arrested after a principal and teacher were shot at a school in southern France on Monday morning.

The 14-year-old entered Lakanal middle school in Aubagne, a small city 11 miles east of Marseille, "with a shotgun inside a guitar case" . He then opened fire before being restrained by a member of staff, regional officials told French media.

No children were harmed and the teachers have been treated for injuries which are not life-threatening, according to Aubagne Mayor Jean-Pierre Squillari, who said the suspect was a pupil in the ninth grade.

The Marseille prosecutor's office has since opened an investigation for attempted murder, it said in a statement.

Local media reported that the incident was not thought to be related to ongoing protests over school conditions, citing sources familiar with the investigation.

The pupil entered school grounds with a gun before several shots were heard, Bouches-du-Rhône departmental council president Martine Vassal told reporters.

The head teacher, 53, was reportedly shot in the leg and lower back, while the 37-year-old teacher's thigh was hit. A third person is said to have sustained minor injuries.

Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said the 14-year-old injured the head and the other teacher on the first floor.

He then went to the second floor and fired twice, "first in front of a teacher towards the floor, and a second time inside an occupied classroom, hitting the chalkboard", Bessone said.

"Neither [that] teacher nor the students were injured, though they were severely shaken."

The boy was restrained by a member of staff in a school corridor, according to the city hall, and taken into police custody.

"All students were immediately confined and made safe within seconds," Squillari, speaking in his role as city mayor, said in an update on social media. A psychological support unit was set up on site to provide emergency support.

Squillari also spoke to reporters and said: "The kids saw practically nothing since it happened in the hallway.

"Psychologically, quite a few were affected, and those in a distressed state are being examined by the psychologist".

He said the suspect was a child "just like any other".

"The father had requested a meeting with the school's educational advisor, but we don't know any more than that," he told broadcaster BFMTV.

Two pupils told BFMTV there was a fire alarm and when they went outside to take the stairs they were told not to go down but they then came face-to-face with the alleged shooter.

On of them explained: "He was a metre away, with his hunting rifle. He fired at the ground."

"We started to run away, but he followed us for a while. We started screaming."

French President Emmanuel Macron posted on X that he extended his "full solidarity and total support" to the teachers, students and parents in shock.

"I salute the composure and exemplary response of the educational team, which made it possible to avoid the worst."

Education Minister Édouard Geffray is due to visit the scene in southern France with Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez..

"Two staff members from the National Education system, a principal and a teacher, were victims this morning of gunshot wounds at Lakanal middle school in Aubagne," Geffray wrote on social media. "A student is said to be the perpetrator."

He added: "This unacceptable act is yet further evidence of the rise of unchecked violence in our society, against which we must all take a stand."

articles.title: HMV to close Oxford Street store after three years
articles.summary: HMV says it is looking for a new site in London's West End, but its current site is "unviable".
articles.body:
HMV has said it will shut its flagship Oxford Street store three years after it reopened the site, blaming a proposed doubling of the rent for the closure.

The entertainment chain said it would leave the shop in March 2027, in a move affecting more than 50 staff.

It said it was looking for a new site in London's West End district for its flagship shop and said it planned to maintain a "significant presence" in the capital.

Phil Halliday, managing director of HMV, said it was "frustrating" that the Oxford Street shop was "commercially unviable".

He said: "This is a special store, it's where we began 100 years ago and bringing it back to life in 2023 was a big moment in our recent history.

"We are looking ahead, and our focus is now on what we do to make exciting steps for HMV in 2027."

The group said its landlords had proposed doubling the rent on the site at 363 Oxford Street, and it was also facing a bill for "substantial" renovation works at the store, which together would make the shop "commercially unsustainable".

HMV said it would look to transfer affected workers to its two other London stores and head office while it looked for a new site.

The chain reopened its historic Oxford Street store in November 2023 after a four-year absence following a deal secured with landlords. It first opened the Oxford Street site in 1921.

HMV has 113 stores across the UK, including six sites under the Fopp brand, as well as another eight in Europe. The group said it remained committed to high street stores.

articles.title: Amritsar airport shuts airspace after drone scare, 2 flights diverted to Delhi, Chandigarh
articles.summary: AMRITSAR: Two flights were diverted after suspected drone activity was reported near Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport in Amritsar around 9.40pm
articles.body: AMRITSAR: Two flights were diverted after suspected drone activity was reported near Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport in Amritsar around 9.40pm on Sunday, prompting authorities to temporarily shut the airspace as a precautionary measure, said Anirudh Sharma, in-charge of Air Traffic Control (ATC).Sharma said Air India flight AI-855, arriving from Delhi, was sent back to Delhi, while IndiGo flight 6E-5028, arriving from Mumbai, was diverted to Chandigarh.The airspace was closed around 9.50pm after information was received about the movement of two to three drones near the airport. Flight operations resumed around 11.15pm following a security review.The incident left several passengers stranded, with some reportedly protesting over the lack of information from officials.A preliminary police investigation indicated that the drones might have been flown to videograph a sports tournament, reportedly a kabaddi competition, in a nearby village. However, drone operations are prohibited within an eight-kilometre radius of the airport.Amritsar Rural SSP Kanwalpreet Singh Chahal said police teams had been deployed in nearby villages and a search operation was under way to ascertain the nature of the drone activity. Further action would be taken based on the findings of the investigation, he said.Police personnel also visited the area as part of the probe. The police appealed to residents not to fly drones without permission, stressing that the airport falls within a high-security zone where such activity is prohibited.A similar incident was reported in September, when as many as five suspected drones were spotted near the airport, forcing seven commercial flights to be diverted to Delhi and Chandigarh.A preliminary inquiry had then indicated that the drones were being used during a sports tournament in a nearby village. articles.title: Lebanon PM vows to track down suspects after truck carrying explosives intercepted
articles.summary: Lebanese authorities is set to launch an extensive investigation to identify and track down suspected members of the militant Hezbollah group, who may be
articles.body: Lebanese authorities is set to launch an extensive investigation to identify and track down suspected members of the militant Hezbollah group, who may be connected to a truck carrying explosives intercepted at the Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint last week, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Monday.Salam termed the incident a “criminal operation” and commended security personnel for stopping the vehicle on the major highway connecting Beirut with the eastern Bekaa Valley.Information minister Paul Morcos said the two individuals detained in connection with the incident had been referred to judicial authorities. He added that security agencies would continue their efforts to identify and apprehend others suspected of involvement.Judicial officials told The Associated Press that the truck was transporting 780 kilograms (1,720 pounds) of explosives. The consignment reportedly included 250 kilograms (550 pounds) of TNT and another 250 kilograms (550 pounds) of C4 plastic explosives.According to the officials, the two detainees claimed they had been instructed to transport the materials from Baalbek, in northeastern Lebanon, to Beirut without being informed of their intended use. They were allegedly supposed to deliver the consignment to a man south of Beirut, identified by the detainees using the nom de guerre Zulfiqar.It remained unclear whether the explosives were intended for use in fibre-optic drones that Hezbollah has been deploying against Israeli troops stationed in parts of southern Lebanon.During a meeting, Salam assured the public that the government would pursue the investigation comprehensively to establish the identities of everyone involved and those directing the operation.“Our government will not tolerate anyone who dares to tamper with the country's security, safety, and stability,” Salam said, according to Morcos.The prime minister also stressed that the government would take decisive measures against the possession, transportation or use of weapons outside state control.For years, Hezbollah was able to move weapons relatively freely in parts of Lebanon. However, the situation changed in March, when the Lebanese government declared all military activities by the Iran-backed group illegal.The decision followed Hezbollah's launch of rockets into northern Israel, triggering a conflict that has killed nearly 4,000 people in Lebanon. The group fired the rockets two days after Israel and the United States began a war against Iran, Hezbollah's principal backer.Morcos said Salam acknowledged public concerns surrounding the intercepted explosives shipment. He also pointed out that C4 had been used in several notorious political assassinations in Lebanon's recent history.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Haunting clues emerge in 7-year fishing boat mystery after wreckage found off island
articles.summary: Green Oceans of Rhode Island says it found the F/V Mistress wreckage just 50 feet from a Block Island Wind Farm turbine, raising questions about the 2019 sinking.
articles.body: An organization believes it has found the wreckage of a fishing boat that sank over seven years ago — potentially solving a mystery surrounding the deaths of two fishermen. Green Oceans, a Rhode Island-based environmental organization, announced the discovery of what it believes is the F/V Mistress in the waters off Block Island in September. The vessel sank Jan. 1, 2019, according to the organization. 118-YEAR-OLD MYSTERY CRACKED AS DIVERS DISCOVER LOST WARSHIP BENEATH THE WAVES Two fishermen died in the incident, and the U.S. Coast Guard searched for the vessel following the sinking but never located the wreckage. The F/V Mistress was discovered approximately 92 feet underwater, just 50 feet from the base of a wind turbine at the Block Island Wind Farm, according to Green Oceans. The organization reported that "apparent human remains" were also found at the site. Michael Lombardi, president of Green Oceans, told Fox News Digital his organization began searching for the vessel after receiving tips from two contractors who had previously worked near turbine No. 1 at the Block Island Wind Farm. One contractor reported hearing rumors of underwater wreckage — while another claimed to have personally spotted wreckage while conducting survey work at the site. "Once plotted on a map, it became obvious where the search area should be focused, and it coincided perfectly with turbine 1," Lombardi said. When asked by Fox News Digital how confident he was that the wreck was the F/V Mistress, Lombardi replied, "100%." He added, "The dive team studied images of the vessel prior to diving the site and were focused on finding key identifying features. … One striking item was the net drum. It has several unique features." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Tim Diaz, who survived the sinking, confirmed that the net drum belonged to the Mistress, according to Lombardi. Diaz built the equipment himself. The mystery isn't over — and Lombardi said there is still some "uncertainty" about what happened in the vessel's final moments, though he said it was undoubtedly in distress. "Based on the orientation of the wreckage on the bottom, there is reason to investigate whether an avoidance maneuver to starboard was made in an attempt to avoid a collision with the turbine," he said. "With the hull full of water, this maneuver could have ultimately caused the vessel to roll and then sink." articles.body: Russia on Monday said it would cease fire for a day so that Ukraine could hold presidential elections, rejecting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's offer for a 60-day truce.Moscow said it wanted an overall peace deal instead.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said President Vladimir Putin would be ready to order the military not to attack Ukraine during its presidential election day. Reuters reported, quoting Peskov's statements from RIA."In the Kremlin, both President ‌Putin ⁠and officials at other levels have repeatedly stated that we do not want a ceasefire," said Peskov. "We want ​long-term ​peace and are ⁠prepared to do everything possible to achieve it."Moscow has repeatedly pressed Kyiv to hold ​elections, calling Zelenskyy an illegitimate ⁠leader.On Sunday, Zelenskyy said that he would organise elections in Ukraine if Russian President Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire, responding to criticism from US President Donald Trump over his leadership."Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections," Zelenskyy told the ABC.Earlier, Trump had criticised Zelenskyy for targeting Russian oil refineries, a day after the United States temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were intended to deprive Moscow of revenue to fund its war in Ukraine."I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump told reporters at the White House.Responding to the remarks, Zelenskyy said the choice of Ukraine's leader rested with its people and noted that Putin would also like to see a change in the country's leadership.Zelenskyy was elected as the President in 2019, meant to serve a standard five-year term which should have ended in 2024. articles.title: 'Gods would be aghast': SC seeks balance between faith and public health in firecracker debate
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday stressed the need to balance religious sentiments with public health concerns while considering restrictions on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday stressed the need to balance religious sentiments with public health concerns while considering restrictions on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR. It said a greater public awareness and voluntary adoption of less polluting practices could offer a way forward.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was not inclined to hurt religious sentiments but emphasised that citizens should be encouraged to celebrate festivals in ways that minimise air and noise pollution."We will not hurt religious sentiments but at the same time, people should themselves come forward and opt for it. The whole exercise should involve a balancing approach," the Chief Justice said, according to news agency PTI.The bench was hearing suo motu proceedings concerning air pollution in the National Capital Region, covering issues including firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management.During the hearing, Justice Bagchi questioned the religious basis for bursting firecrackers, asking, "What is religious about bursting crackers?"Senior advocate Aparajita Singh, who is assisting the bench as amicus curiae, highlighted the health risks associated with air pollution, particularly for children, elderly people and those with existing health vulnerabilities."Gods would be aghast if they knew that children were suffering and getting sick in their name," Singh said, responding to arguments linking firecrackers with religious practices, PTI reported.She also flagged difficulties in enforcing restrictions on the duration of firecracker use, arguing that limits on the number of hours allowed would have little impact without effective implementation."It sounds really nice in court, that it is only two hours or one hour. But the court also knows that it is not implemented. It is impossible for police officers to be on every street all the time," Singh said.The amicus suggested referring the issue to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), the statutory body responsible for air quality management in the region, so that it could examine the available material and associated medical concerns.The bench, however, cautioned against issuing directions that might be difficult to implement on the ground."We have to be extremely careful in passing an order unless we are in a position to make it manageable and enforceable," the Chief Justice said, adding that restrictive directions were often perceived as coercive.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: PM believes Brexit vote was legitimate despite Russia interference claims, No 10 says
articles.summary: It is "inconceivable" that Russia did not try to use the referendum to its advantage, No 10 said, but the PM believed it did not succeed in influencing the result.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham believes the 2016 Brexit referendum result was "legitimate", Downing Street has said, after the prime minister claimed there was Russian interference in the vote.

It is "inconceivable" that Russia did not try to use the referendum to its advantage, a No 10 spokesman said, but the PM believed it did not succeed in influencing the result.

Burnham told The Rest is Politics podcast, that upon arriving in Downing Street, he had asked if there had been Russian interference in the vote, adding: "I've had the clear answer that, yes, there was."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called the prime minister a "liar" while the Conservatives said he had been "at best... carelessly vague".

Former prime minister Boris Johnson wrote on X that in 2016, when he became foreign secretary the security services had told him "there was no evidence of any successful interference in the 2016 referendum, by Russia or any other power".

He added: "Either the security services have changed their view - which would be very odd - or Burnham is lying about what he has been told."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey backed Burnham, posting on social media: "This statement needed to be said by a prime minister. After the Conservatives suppressed the truth for years, this took courage."

In his podcast interview, Burnham said there was "certainly misinformation, disinformation that is emanating from Russia into German politics".

He added: "I think we've been too much on the back foot on that actually and we haven't informed people sufficiently about the extent to which people are seeking to disrupt the political process from overseas."

The prime minister did not go into further detail about the nature or extent of Russian activities during the 2016 referendum.

Speaking to broadcasters on Monday morning, Foreign Minister Stephen Doughty would not provide specific details about interference in the vote but said Russia had been "attempting to interfere in a series of democratic events".

Later on Monday, after being pressed several times on whether the PM believes the Brexit result was legitimate, the No 10 spokesman said: "Yes we believe the referendum result was legitimate."

He added: "The PM absolutely accepts the referendum result."

The prime minister's initial comments on Russia prompted an angry reaction from some Brexit supporters.

Farage, who was a prominent Brexit campaigner, said: "The prime minister is a liar, yes, a liar."

"There was no Russian interference - the Russian hoax has run all the way through this," he added.

"This is out-of-touch, out-of-date Andy Burnham with all sorts of bizarre ideas."

Conservative shadow minister Katie Lam said the prime minister "risks sowing doubt about the result of a professionally-run, independently-monitored democratic vote".

In a letter to Communities Secretary Angela Rayner, Lam also suggested Burnham could purposely be seeking to cast doubt on the legitimacy in order to justify his efforts to build a closer relationship with the EU.

Burnham says it is 'clear' Russia interfered with Brexit vote

Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

In 2020, a parliamentary report did not reach a firm conclusion on whether Russia had tried to intervene in UK elections and referendums, but criticised the government for failing to fully assess and counter the threat from Russian 'troll' accounts on social media.

Report chair Stewart Hosie accused the government of having "actively avoided" looking for evidence of interference.

Asked in 2017, if he had seen evidence of Russia successfully meddling in UK elections, then-Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson said: "Nyet [Russian for no], not a sausage."

Earlier this year, the government published an independent review on foreign influence in UK politics which said there were attempts to "sow distrust and exacerbate divisions in UK society with the ultimate aim of undermining confidence in our democracy".

Report author Philip Rycroft said it was difficult to establish the impact of these efforts and that the public "can be credited with sufficient common sense to see of the more egregious attempts to suborn their opinions".

However, he added that while there was no "immediate crisis" in British democracy "there is no guarantee that this will persist".

articles.title: Becky Hill is latest headliner for Ludlow Castle gigs
articles.summary: The singer is the latest act to be announced for a series of concerts at the castle next summer.
articles.body:
Becky Hill will appear at Ludlow castle next summer, as part of the venue's annual concert series.

The two-time BRIT Award winner, famous for songs including Gecko, Remember and Lose Control will appear on 23 July.

The singer is the second act to be revealed, following the announcement that McFly will appear at the venue two days later.

The Live at Ludlow Castle events have been running since 2023 and this summer 50,000 people visited over two weekends.

Hill was born and raised less than 20 miles away, in Bewdley, and the event organisers, Futuresound Group, described her as "one of the stand-out talents in British dance music".

Her third album, Rebecca, is due to be released in November.

Tickets will go on sale to people in the Ludlow area from Wednesday and then on general sale from Friday.

This summer, eight open-air shows at the castle featured artists including Snow Patrol, Paul Weller, The Human League, Tom Grennan, The Streets, Rick Astley, Richard Ashcroft and Scissor Sisters.

They were supported by Corinne Bailey Rae, Miles Kane, Marc Almond, The Lightning Seeds, Heather Small and CAST as well as up and coming acts such as Ellur, The Florentinas, Versaints and more.

The concerts at the castle have a capacity of 6,000 and have gradually increased in number.

An agreement was signed this summer to continue them until at least 2033.

Futuresound said they brought more than £1m into the town in 2025.

Earlier this year, Ian Evans, chair of Ludlow Chamber of Trade and Commerce said his shop saw a 25% increase in trade while the concerts were on and described them as a "massive event" for the town.

articles.title: Stinky American plant cleared from Buckinghamshire river
articles.summary: The plant is said to smell like "rotting meat" and is is native to swamps and other wetlands in the Pacific Northwest.
articles.body:
An invasive plant said to smell like "rotting meat" has been cleared from a Buckinghamshire river.

More than 2.5km (1.6 miles) of the River Alderbourne has been treated for American skunk cabbage, which is native to swamps and other wetlands in the Pacific Northwest.

BBC Gardeners' World Magazine has described the plant as having a smell that resembles "rotting meat".

Environmental charity Groundwork South received £9,900 from Affinity Water's INNS Out Scheme to carry out the work.

The team surveyed and treated several locations, including a site at Harding's Row Nature Reserve near Iver Heath.

Surveys conducted after the work showed "promising early results", according to the charity.

Matt Mountain, senior project manager at Groundwork, said: "The support from Affinity has been crucial in allowing us to tackle this relatively new invasive species before it reaches a stage where eradication becomes impractical.

"It's a real win for local and regional wildlife and the wider ecosystem. This is especially true here in the Colne catchment as the rivers under threat are globally significant chalk streams."

articles.title: In 1967, Martin Luther King Jr. preached at Cleveland's Shiloh Baptist Church; the historic congregation now has a $750,000 grant to repair its building and improve access for the community
articles.summary: In 1967, Martin Luther King Jr. stood at the pulpit of Shiloh Baptist Church in Cleveland, Ohio, speaking about the Vietnam War and civil rights.
articles.body: In 1967, Martin Luther King Jr. stood at the pulpit of Shiloh Baptist Church in Cleveland, Ohio, speaking about the Vietnam War and civil rights. Nearly six decades later, the historic African American congregation has secured a $750,000 grant to repair its building and make it more accessible to the community. According to News 5 Cleveland, the funding comes through the National Park Service’s African American Civil Rights Grant Program, with the Cleveland Restoration Society helping the church prepare its application. The grant will support essential repairs while helping Shiloh continue its work as a place of worship, community service and civil rights history.A congregation with roots in 1849Shiloh Baptist Church was founded in 1849 and is described by News 5 Cleveland as the city’s oldest African American Baptist congregation. After occupying several locations over the years, it moved into its current building on Scovill Avenue in 1926. The historic structure had previously housed B’nai Jeshurun Temple and is recognised as a local and national historic landmark.For generations, Shiloh has served more than its own congregation. Its history is tied to the experiences of African Americans who moved north during the Great Migration, as well as to Cleveland’s civil rights movement. The church provided a place for worship, support and advocacy during periods of social change.Its community role was also evident during the Hough riots of 1966, when the congregation helped rebuild homes destroyed by fire. That history reflects the church’s involvement in neighbourhood life beyond Sunday services, including efforts to support residents facing hardship.Martin Luther King Jr.’s visit in 1967One of the most significant moments in Shiloh’s history came in 1967, when Martin Luther King Jr. visited Cleveland and preached from its pulpit. According to News 5 Cleveland, the visit was his final one to the city before his assassination in 1968. The Rev. Dr. Lisa Goods, Shiloh’s current pastor and the first woman to lead the congregation, told the broadcaster that King spoke about the Vietnam War and delivered a version of his “A Knock at Midnight” speech. He also called on the congregation to support Operation Breadbasket and protest Sealtest over its treatment of African Americans.The visit connected the church to the wider struggle for racial equality at a time when civil rights activism and opposition to the Vietnam War were prominent issues in the United States. Preserving the building therefore means maintaining a physical place associated with a significant chapter in Cleveland’s history. Shiloh also has cultural connections beyond the civil rights movement. Goods told News 5 Cleveland that actress and singer Dorothy Dandridge was a member of the congregation and had credited the church with hosting her first performance. During the Harlem Renaissance, the church also hosted artistic activity, adding another dimension to its cultural legacy.What the $750,000 grant will fundThe National Park Service included Shiloh Baptist Church’s rehabilitation among the projects receiving funding through its African American Civil Rights Preservation and History Grants. Its published awards list identifies the Cleveland Restoration Society as the recipient organisation for the $750,000 Shiloh Baptist Church Rehabilitation project.According to News 5 Cleveland, the money will address several problems affecting the building. Planned work includes restoring the deteriorating portico, repairing water-damaged plaster throughout the church, installing air conditioning in the sanctuary and adding an elevator to improve accessibility. These improvements are intended to protect the historic structure while making it easier for people to use. Repairing damaged areas can help preserve the building for the future, while air conditioning and an elevator can make the space more comfortable and accessible to a wider range of visitors.The grant will also support an update to the church’s National Register of Historic Places nomination, which was originally completed in 1982. The revised documentation is expected to better reflect Shiloh’s history and its role in the civil rights movement.Keeping the church active in the communityThe Cleveland Restoration Society worked with Shiloh on the grant application. Its president, Kathleen Crowther, described the funding as an important opportunity for urban congregations trying to maintain historic buildings. Churches can face significant financial pressure when older structures need major repairs, particularly when congregations have limited resources.The application also highlighted Shiloh’s ongoing community work, including programmes related to health services, food access and youth outreach. The church has also received a grant for a feasibility study exploring affordable housing on some of its vacant land.For Goods, the funding offers a chance to protect the building while sustaining the congregation’s broader purpose. The aim is not simply to preserve an old structure, but to keep it useful to the people it serves.Preserving history for the next generationThe National Park Service’s grant programme supports projects that preserve places and stories connected to the African American struggle for civil rights. Shiloh’s award places the Cleveland congregation among efforts to protect buildings that carry both architectural and historical importance.With repairs, improved accessibility and updated historical documentation planned, the grant could help ensure that the church remains a living community space rather than just a landmark from the past. Nearly 60 years after King preached there, Shiloh Baptist Church is preparing for its next chapter while safeguarding the history that made it significant.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2020, a Kansas couple received a permit for a wedding venue without sprinklers; after a two-year delay and a code change, they claimed more than $550,000 in losses, and an appeals court has revived one claim
articles.summary: A couple in Kansas, United States, who planned to build a wedding venue have received another opportunity to pursue part of their legal case against
articles.body: A couple in Kansas, United States, who planned to build a wedding venue have received another opportunity to pursue part of their legal case against Leavenworth County. George Daniel Lynch and Cynthia Lynch, who own Whiskey Ridge, LLC, had sought damages of at least $550,000 after a dispute over building permits and fire safety requirements. The Kansas Court of Appeals has now ruled that one of their constitutional claims can proceed, while upholding the dismissal of their other claims.According to the court documents, the dispute began in April 2020, when the couple's business received a special use permit to build a wedding venue. At the time, the permit did not require the proposed building to have a fire suppression sprinkler system. However, construction did not begin immediately because of the COVID-19 pandemic.More than two years later, when the business approached the county for a building permit, it was informed that its original special use permit had expired. During that period, the county had also adopted a building code requiring sprinkler systems in buildings such as the proposed venue. This meant Whiskey Ridge could no longer proceed under the conditions of its original permit.The disagreement eventually reached the courts, with the couple and their businesses accusing the county of unfair treatment and seeking compensation for the additional expenses they claimed to have incurred. On Friday, the Kansas Court of Appeals partly overturned an earlier decision dismissing the case, allowing the couple's equal protection claim to move forward.Two-year delay changed plansAccording to the court's opinion, Whiskey Ridge received its original special use permit in April 2020. The proposed venue was to be built mainly from steel and concrete, with some wood used in its construction. The permit did not include a requirement for a sprinkler system.However, the pandemic delayed construction for more than two years. When Whiskey Ridge returned in mid-2022 to seek a building permit, county officials informed the business that its earlier special use permit had lapsed and that a new one would be required.Another change had taken place in the meantime. In December 2020, Leavenworth County adopted the 2006 International Building Code, which required buildings such as the planned wedding venue to have fire suppression sprinklers.Whiskey Ridge sought an exemption from this requirement through the County Board of Building Codes Appeals. The board rejected its request.Despite the disagreement, the business went ahead with construction. The county subsequently issued temporary permits allowing the venue to operate without sprinklers, provided a firetruck and personnel were present during events.The county commission later rejected the business's application for a new special use permit without the sprinkler requirement. Whiskey Ridge eventually installed the system, after which the county approved a new permit.Couple sought more than $550,000Whiskey Ridge claimed that the county's decisions had caused substantial additional expenses. Its legal complaint linked those costs to the refusal to recognise the original permit, the rejection of its request for an exemption and the conditions imposed on its temporary operations.The plaintiffs also alleged that two senior county employees had indicated that a sprinkler system would not be necessary if the business obtained a variance or waiver from the state fire marshal.According to their allegations, they obtained the required relief, but county commissioner Mike Stieben and others subsequently influenced the state fire marshal to withdraw it.These allegations formed part of the business's claims that officials had improperly interfered with its business interests.The lawsuit sought compensatory damages of "not less than $550,000." However, the district court dismissed all the claims. Whiskey Ridge then appealed that decision.Appeals court allowed one claim tThe Kansas Court of Appeals examined several legal claims, including alleged interference with business interests, unequal treatment, violation of substantive due process rights and unlawful taking of property.The judges found that Whiskey Ridge had failed to pursue available legal remedies against certain county decisions within the required time. Kansas law generally provides 30 days to challenge the relevant zoning and county commission decisions in district court.Because Whiskey Ridge had not taken those steps, the appeals court upheld the dismissal of its three tortious interference claims. It directed, however, that those claims be dismissed without prejudice rather than with prejudice. The court reached a different conclusion on the equal protection claim.Whiskey Ridge had alleged that another wedding venue, operating from a refurbished building made mainly of wood, had been allowed to obtain a special use permit without installing a sprinkler system.The judges found that this comparison was sufficient for the equal protection claim to proceed at the initial stage of litigation. They also concluded that the district court had applied an incorrect procedural standard when assessing the claim. The appeals court therefore ordered the equal protection claim to be reinstated.What happens next ?The ruling does not mean that Whiskey Ridge has proved the county treated it unlawfully or that it is entitled to the compensation it requested.The appeals court upheld the dismissal of the substantive due process claim and the claim that the county had unlawfully taken a protected property interest.On the property claim, the judges noted that county regulations treated a special use permit as abandoned if the permitted activity had ceased for 12 consecutive months. Because Whiskey Ridge had not acted on its original permit for approximately two years, the court concluded that the county had properly considered it abandoned.The case will now return to the district court for further proceedings on the equal protection claim. The lower court must also amend its judgment to reflect that the tortious interference claims were dismissed without prejudice.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Shadrack Sibiya leaves SAPS: Dishonourable discharge for South Africa's deputy police chief
articles.summary: Shadrack Sibiya had denied grooming a 16-year-old and raping an 18-year-old.
articles.body:
South Africa's deputy police chief has resigned three weeks after he was charged with sexual offences.

A lawyer representing Lt Gen Shadrack Sibiya submitted his resignation letter at his disciplinary hearing on Monday, a police spokesperson said.

The charges relate to allegations that he sexually groomed a 16-year-old girl and raped an 18-year-old woman. He is also facing a charge of trafficking.

Sibiya has denied all the charges. He says he did have sex with the 18 year-old but says it was consensual.

He has been in custody since he was arrested three weeks ago after his bail application was denied.

The case comes as the police service is in the spotlight at a major public inquiry over allegations of corruption and collusion with criminals.

The inquiry, known as the Madlanga Commission, began in September 2025 and has heard accusations that Sibiya received a gift of 20 impalas from an alleged criminal kingpin in exchange for a police contract.

articles.title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
articles.summary: Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
articles.body:
Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.

Hackers reportedly gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight.

The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack.

More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while at least 300 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, according to the AFP news agency.

Intermarché said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.

Some supermarket staff reportedly said they were hit by waves of hot air when they opened freezer units on Monday morning.

French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C.

Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of €270,000 (£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions.

The Paris prosecutor's office told AFP it had opened an investigation into the incident, which it called a "large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France".

Eoropean Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: "Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality."

The full scale of the attack is so far unclear.

Reports in specialist retail and local media said stores from other food giants, including Carrefour, E.Leclerc and Monoprix, were also attacked. BBC News has approached the supermarket chains for comment.

In a post on X, Coopérative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were "fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible".

He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was "unacceptable".

articles.title: Social media star from Jersey joins Blue Peter
articles.summary: Leo Olsson joins the series after building an online following doing "bucket list" challenges.
articles.body:
A social media star from Jersey has been unveiled as the newest presenter of Blue Peter.

Leo Olsson is best known for documenting "bucket list" personal challenges online, where he has almost 500,000 followers.

His first Blue Peter episode is due to be broadcast on November 20.

Olsson said: "It's a privilege to join a programme with such an incredible legacy".

Growing up in Jersey, Olsson started making videos when he was 12 years old.

As a teenager, he became well-known locally after writing letters to world leaders , seeking their best words of wisdom.

His desire to become a filmmaker lead him to a career as a content-creator, amassing more than 13 million likes and more than 454,000 followers across social media platforms.

Videos followed him as he took on challenges such as learning to play the piano, riding a unicycle and building a surfboard from scratch.

Speaking about joining the programme, he said : "There's no other show in the world like Blue Peter. It's all about adventure and not being afraid to try new things."

"Where else would you find a presenter trying to cross the Irish Sea in a Zorb ball, or walk a tightrope between the chimneys of Battersea Power Station?

"Growing up, all of my role models were the people I watched online and on television, so now I want show kids that you can go out and do whatever you want to do, take on a challenge, big or small."

In his first Blue Peter appearance, due to be broadcast on CBBC on Friday 20 November, Leo will earn his Blue Peter badge by joining a formation skydive being awarded his badge 4,000ft in the air.

Programme bosses described him as having "a sense of adventure and positivity" that made him the "perfect fit for Blue Peter".

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court against alleged electoral irregularities encountered police barricades in central
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court against alleged electoral irregularities encountered police barricades in central Delhi on Monday before the opposition leaders eventually reached the court and filed a joint petition against the Election Commission of India (EC).The march, dubbed "March for Democracy", brought together opposition leaders, MPs, party workers and activists, with Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav among those who joined the procession.The march was initially halted at Bhagwan Dass Road, where police had erected barricades to prevent the procession from proceeding towards the Supreme Court. As the crowd swelled and the standoff continued, several leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav, climbed atop a vehicle as supporters raised slogans against the government and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.As per Supreme Court website, their legal team had filed the petition against the EC as the leaders failed to reach on time.Subsequently they reached the Supreme Court premises and filed the petition in a show of strenght. Visuals released by the news agency showed Rahul Gandhi, Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filing the plea.The march came after the Chief Justice of India refused to meet the opposition leaders who had sought an appointment to submit a memorandum over alleged electoral irregularities. CJI Surya Kant had said the matter was already before the court and advised the leaders to pursue the judicial route by filing a petition.ALSO READ: 'Ready to contest on ballot paper': Himanta lobs dare at Cong but with a big rider11 leaders named in the petitionThe petition names Rahul Gandhi as the lead petitioner, along with 10 other opposition leaders from INDIA bloc parties. The petitioners are:Rahul Gandhi, CongressMallikarjun Kharge, CongressSaugata Roy, Mamata-TMCAkhilesh Yadav, Samajwadi PartyTejashwi Prasad Yadav, Rashtriya Janata DalSanjay Raut, Shiv Sena (UBT)MA Baby, CPMD Raja, CPIMahua Majhi, Jharkhand Mukti MorchaSupriya Sule, NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)ET Mohammed Basheer, Indian Union Muslim League leaderThe Election Commission of India has been named as a respondent. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the other two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, have also been named as respondents, according to the Supreme Court website.What does the petition seekThe petition filed by Rahul Gandhi and 10 other opposition leaders in the Supreme Court has challenged the manner in which the Election Commission has taken decisions relating to the SIR of electoral rolls, news agency ANI reported.It seeks disclosure of the EC’s complete files, agendas, minutes, notings and objections concerning the disputed decisions, including the June 24, 2025 decision to commence the SIR, as well as ECINET and ERONET access logs.It also seeks a judicial examination of whether these decisions were taken in accordance with Article 324 of the Constitution, the 2023 law governing the Election Commission and the Supreme Court’s ruling in TN Seshan vs Union of India.The petition seeks several safeguards against voter deletions during the SIR, including a direction that no elector be removed from the electoral roll without prior notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard. It also seeks the booth-wise publication of deleted electors, along with the reasons for their deletion and demographic details.The petition further calls for an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to audit deletions and modifications in electoral-roll databases, including ECINET and ERONET. It also seeks an interim suspension of the ongoing SIR until the court adjudicates the matter.Additionally, the plea asks the court to direct the Election Commission to ensure that “every decision of the Election Commission relating to the Special Intensive Revision is taken and duly minuted” in accordance with the 2023 Act.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Nidal Hasan execution - why US is bringing back firing squads
articles.summary: Medical experts and those who study the death penalty say each method can go wrong and cause severe pain.
articles.body:
Warning: this story contains upsetting descriptions of executions

America's use of the death penalty is under the spotlight once again after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the military would livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan.

The former military psychiatrist fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at the Fort Hood military base in Texas in 2009.

His execution would be the first time the US Army had used a firing squad since 1945, a method that several states already authorise to put people to death.

And it comes on the heels of the botched death by lethal injection of Christa Pike - a woman convicted of murdering her classmate.

Pike was taken to hospital and then discharged to prison 10 days later, after making a recovery from the failed attempt, her lawyers said.

Amid rising concerns over botched executions - and renewed federal support for the death penalty - the US has introduced both new and old forms of execution like firing squads, the electric chair and the gas chamber.

The vast majority of executions in the US have been lethal injections since they were first introduced in Texas in 1982. The Death Penalty Information Center, a non-profit think tank that does not take a stance on the death penalty, says that there have been 64 botched executions over the past 50 years - including 51 botched lethal injections - out of a total of 1,683 executions.

The difficulty of carrying out these executions, and the uproar over what some perceive as inhumane treatment, has led officials to consider alternative methods of putting people to death. But medical experts and those who study executions say every method the US uses to put people to death can result in severe pain, especially when botched.

"We always have the possibility that there's going to be a mistake made when human beings are involved in executions," said Robin Maher, the executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center.

Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago - why are they resuming now?

Several medical groups - including the national associations for doctors and nurses - also ban their members from participating in executions. The American Medical Association, which represents doctors in the US, states they are "a profession dedicated to preserving life when there is hope of doing so" and that participating in any way in executions is antithetical to their oath.

Lethal injection, which was first used in Texas in 1982, is now the most common way people are executed across the US, with many states making it their default method.

Dr Joel Zivot, a professor of anaesthesiology and surgery based in Atlanta, Georgia, said states turned to lethal injection because it appeared from the outside to be a more peaceful means of execution.

Dr Zivot said that sometimes the injection of the drugs can cause pulmonary edema, when a person's lungs fill with fluid, which can give people the painful sensation of drowning.

"It's a terrifying way to die - to drown," he said.

Other times, people have medical conditions, like Pike - who suffered from thrombocytosis and other medical problems her lawyers warned about - that can complicate the execution and make it more painful.

During Pike's failed execution, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

There are a host of reasons why so many lethal injections have been botched, but some of the same factors persist, said Maher.

"Oftentimes, the executions go wrong because training of staff is inadequate, because drugs are degraded or expired or improperly stored, or because states are experimenting with different combinations of drugs that have never been used before," she said.

Most of the time, little information is available to the public about the people administering the lethal injection, as the states do not usually share what training they have had.

"We have discovered that in many instances, and unfortunately subsequent to a botched execution, that the cause was the inadequate experience and training of the execution staff," Maher said.

Drugs for lethal injections are also hard to obtain because many pharmaceutical companies do not want to sell the medications to prisons for that use, since they were developed for life-saving purposes.

In light of many of these challenges, some states have turned to executing people with a new and controversial method: nitrogen gas.

Alabama and Louisiana are the first states to have carried out executions with nitrogen gas, though three other states - Arkansas, Mississippi and Oklahoma - also allow for it.

Two years ago, Alabama used nitrogen gas to execute Kenneth Eugene Smith, after a botched attempt to put him to death via lethal injection in 2022.

During the execution, which took 25 minutes, Smith thrashed violently on the gurney as he was given the gas, a witness told the BBC at the time.

The method involves forcing a prisoner to breathe pure nitrogen gas until they suffocate.

Dr Zivot said people who breathe in the gas sometimes get seizures. Alabama has executed seven people using nitrogen gas since introducing the method in January 2024.

"Each time it was a horror show of struggling, of moving, of seizing," Dr Zivot said.

While some states have explored new methods, others have reauthorised some of the earliest ways US officials used to put people to death.

As of this year, nine states have approved execution by electric chair, with South Carolina using it as their default method.

Electrocution "has a horrible history of botched executions", Maher said, and errors with these executions is one of the reasons why states introduced lethal injections in the first place.

In 1997, Pedro Medina's head caught fire as he was put to death in an electric chair in Florida.

"A solid flame covered his whole head, from one side to the other. I had the impression of somebody being burned alive," his attorney Mike Minerva said, according to the Los Angeles Times.

A method once used as punishment in the military and in times of war, firing squad executions have also proven susceptible to human error.

Mikahl Mahdi was executed by a three-person firing squad last year after admitting to killing an off-duty police officer in 2004. But his lawyers say his death was prolonged because the bullets missed his heart and instead hit his liver and other organs.

In July, Idaho became the first state to use a firing squad as its primary method of execution after it ran into issues with lethal injections. Mississippi, Oklahoma, Utah and South Carolina also authorise this execution method.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former US Army sergeant who survived being shot seven times by Hasan in the Fort Hood attack, told the BBC the firing squad was a "befitting" method to end his life because lethal injection and a gas chamber would be "doing him a favour".

Hanging was the main method of execution in the US until the 1890s, and several Asian countries including Japan and Singapore still use this method. But in the US, no states authorise hanging because of its "terrible" history, Maher said.

"Hanging has such a terrible association with racial violence and lynching in the states," she said. "So that is why there's no state that's using hanging or has authorised that method to be used."

Trump - a proponent of the death penalty - brought back the federal death penalty when he returned to office in 2025, after Joe Biden's administration put a moratorium on federal executions in 2021.

"Capital punishment is an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens," his office wrote in an executive order.

Maher said there has been "quite a bit of activity" in state legislatures to approve and reauthorise other methods of execution since Trump began expressing enthusiasm for the death penalty.

Trump has called for the death penalty to be expanded to punish large-scale drug dealers, human traffickers and those who kill police officers. Over the past 50 years, all prisoners who received death sentences were convicted of murder, though capital punishment was also used for rape convictions before that.

Asked by reporters whether Pike's failed lethal injection should spur changes to the death penalty, Trump did not directly answer the question, adding that the execution method "shouldn't be very difficult".

articles.title: Trump critic Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home searched by federal agents
articles.summary: US authorities searched the Democratic congresswoman’s home as part of a criminal investigation.
articles.body:
United States federal agents have searched the Washington, DC-area home of Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar, a vocal critic of President Donald Trump, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.

Agents from Homeland Security Investigations carried out the search early Monday morning, according to The Associated Press news agency, citing two people familiar with the matter.

The Justice Department confirmed that agents had executed a court-authorised search warrant in the US capital but did not identify Omar or provide details about the investigation.

Fox News reported, citing unidentified sources, that the search was linked to allegations of immigration fraud involving paperwork submitted by Omar’s late father when she was a child. Omar has previously denied allegations of immigration fraud, and no charges have been announced.

The Somali-born congresswoman, who represents a district in the state of Minnesota that includes Minneapolis, has long been a target of Trump’s political attacks, particularly over immigration. Vice President JD Vance previously accused Omar of immigration fraud without providing evidence and said the administration was looking into how to investigate her.

Omar has dismissed the allegations as politically motivated. The search comes just over three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, when Republicans will be fighting to retain control of Congress.

articles.title: 3 masked thieves in women’s nightwear prise open ATM, steal cash
articles.summary: Masked thieves in women’s nightwear cut open SBI ATM in Gandhari, Telangana with gas cutter, fleeing with suspected Rs 25 lakh; police probe CCTV.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Three men wearing women’s nightwear and masks allegedly broke into a State Bank of India (SBI) ATM in Gandhari mandal headquarters in the early hours of Sunday and fled with cash after cutting open the cash-dispensing machine with a gas cutter. Police suspect that around Rs 25 lakh may have been stolen, though the exact amount is yet to be ascertained.According to police, the three men arrived at the ATM centre in a vehicle shortly after 1am on Sunday. While one of them stood guard outside, the other two entered the kiosk and used a gas cutter to prise open the ATM. They then took the cash and fled.The theft came to light on Sunday morning when locals noticed the damaged ATM and alerted police, who reached the spot and collected details about the incident.Police are examining CCTV footage from the ATM centre and surrounding areas to identify the suspects and trace their movements. Footage from cameras inside the centre reportedly captured two men in nightwearcutting open the ATM and fleeing with the cash. Their identities and the place from where they arrived were yet to be established.Gandhari police station sub-inspector M Mahender said preliminary information suggests that the ATM operators deposited around Rs 30 lakh into the machine at about 1pm on Friday. Customers are believed to have withdrawn around Rs 5 lakh by midnight on Saturday, leaving approximately Rs 25 lakh in the machine. articles.title: Trichy corporation begins road patchwork at Rs 1.7 crore
articles.summary: Trichy Corporation starts Rs 1.7 crore patchwork on 298.7 km of damaged roads across 54 wards, aiming to finish repairs in a week before monsoon.
articles.body: Trichy: Trichy corporation on Monday began patchwork of damaged tar and cement concrete roads to overcome inundation threats before the onset of the northeast monsoon. The local body has allocated Rs 1.7 crore to improve the conditions of 298.7-km-long roads.Officials said a total of 443 works have been approved by commissioner N Ponmani, allocating Rs 39.4 lakh for zone I, Rs 27.5 lakh for zone II, Rs 37.5 lakh for zone III, Rs 40.2 lakh for zone IV, and Rs 28.5 lakh for zone V. The work will cover 54 wards out of a total of 65, particularly covering the areas such as Thillai Nagar, Woraiyur, Thennur, Kattur, KK Nagar and Palakkarai where ongoing UGD works have damaged several portions of roads.“On busy arterial roads and commercial streets, workers have been engaged at night to cover the potholes,” an official said. The proposed road repair works are likely to be completed in a week.Even for minor patches, officials added that compactors have been deployed to level the patched area to avoid level differences between the old surfaces and patched spots.
